answer: The estimated interaction OR between BCG vaccination status and prior medical history on COVID-19 severity is 1.17 (exp(coef=0.1571)), 95% CI 0.73-1.88, p=0.52 — a small, non-statistically-significant interaction in this synthetic sample. Under the primary proportional-odds ordinal model (severity = max AE grade over RTI events, 0 = no RTI; predictors BCG × prior-medical-history + patients_seen + expect_interact; statsmodels OrderedModel, logit), the OR for higher severity with BCG (vs placebo) is 1.16 among those without prior medical history and 1.36 among those with it — i.e., the BCG-vs-placebo association is ~17% larger in subjects with prior medical history, but the effect is not significant (LL=-1127.07, null LL=-1150.94, LR=47.74). Plain language: BCG vaccination's association with COVID-19-related severity did not differ meaningfully by prior medical history — the multiplicative interaction OR of 1.17 is close to 1 with a wide confidence interval spanning no effect, so there is no convincing evidence of an interaction.
